  • An action protocol must be applied by schools when the CO2 standard is exceeded.
  • Every classroom must have an air exchanger or purifier, supplied and paid for by the department, within 12 months.

25793:
• This bill strengthens State secularism in Québec's public and private schools.
  • It requires several people in schools to have their face uncovered and expands the ban on religious symbols.
Part 1 Education Act
  • The public school system must respect democratic values, equality between men and women, and State secularism.
  • Students must have their face uncovered in schools, vocational training centres, and adult education centres.
  • Children schooled at home and their parents must also have their face uncovered when receiving services offered by the school service centre.
  • Anyone providing services to students or in contact with them in a school must have their face uncovered.
  • Students must respect equality between men and women and must not bully others based on race, sexual orientation, gender, disability, or other grounds.
  • Vocational training centres and adult education centres must also adopt codes of conduct.
  • The ban on wearing religious symbols is extended to more staff members and to certain people under a service contract.
  • Employees already employed or under contract before the bill is passed are not subject to this new ban.
  • The rules for requesting a religious accommodation involving an absence from work are clarified and regulated.
  • No religious accommodation is allowed when it affects the duty to attend school.
  • People who provide services to students, as well as members of governing boards and boards of directors, must act without religious considerations.
  • Staff of school service centres must base their statements and decisions on State secularism.
  • School service centres must adopt a code of ethics for members of governing boards.
  • School and centre premises can no longer be used for religious practices.
  • It is prohibited to try to influence, for religious reasons, the exercise of a power or duty provided for by law.
  • Teachers must submit a teaching plan to their principal, who must evaluate them every year.
  • A new committee on the quality of educational services is created to help school administrations.
  • The minister may set the schedule for exams and order a school service centre to comply with an act or regulation.
  • Certain decisions made by the minister, such as suspending or revoking a teaching permit, apply even if the person challenges them before the Administrative Tribunal of Québec.
  • Staff of French-language school service centres must communicate only in French with students and among colleagues.
Part 2 Act respecting private education
  • Staff members of private schools not recognized for subsidy purposes must also have their face uncovered.
Part 3 Education Act and Act respecting private education
  • Schools must include these requirements in their codes of conduct.
  • Certain rules in this bill apply even if they conflict with certain rights under the charters.
Part 4 Regulation respecting ethics and professional conduct standards
  • Technical adjustment for consistency concerning members of the boards of directors of French-language school service centres.

26675:
• This bill puts in place several measures from the March 25, 2025 budget and amends 38 laws and regulations.
  • It affects, among other things, pensions, vehicle registration, child and spousal support, municipal taxation and life insurance.
Part 1 Act respecting the Québec Pension Plan
  • Work is only considered to be done in Québec if it is done in Canada, for the purpose of calculating pensions.
  • Months during which a person receives a reduced CNESST benefit no longer count in calculating their pension.
Part 2 Highway Safety Code
  • The vehicle value threshold triggering an additional registration fee rises from $40,000 to $62,500.
  • Electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles lose their exemption from this fee for values between $40,000 and $75,000.
  • A new additional fee applies specifically to electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles for their registration.
Part 3 Act respecting the Institut de la statistique du Québec
  • Clarifies the rules when the Institute collects information for a public body.
  • More researchers linked to a public body will be able to access information held by the Institute for research purposes.
Part 4 Code of Civil Procedure
  • Changes how the portion of a support-paying parent's income that can be seized is calculated, and the seizure rate.
  • Child support payments for an adult child can no longer be seized from the parent who receives them.
Part 5 Act to facilitate the payment of support
  • A parent who receives last-resort financial assistance no longer has to provide a guarantee for the collection of their support payments.
  • In a state of emergency, the Minister of Finance will be able to adjust collection fees and advances paid to parents owed support.
Part 6 Tax Administration Act
  • The calculation used to determine whether a business is a "large corporation" will take into account the capital of related businesses.
  • Revenu Québec will be able to share certain tax information, without the person's consent, with the Minister of Finance to help prepare economic policies.
Part 7 Act respecting insurers
  • Life insurers will be able to obtain information from Revenu Québec and the Registrar of Civil Status to notify beneficiaries that they may be owed money after a death.
Part 8 Act respecting municipal taxation
  • Municipalities will no longer be able to impose a business tax on companies, except for certain assessments by business development corporations.
  • Municipalities will no longer be able to establish a rental value roll for buildings.
Part 9 Various measures
  • Funding for the Fonds Avenir Mécénat Culture increases.
  • The fee to consult the land register is revised.
  • Québec's debt reduction targets are raised for 2032-2033 and 2037-2038.
  • The government will be able to change parental insurance plan contribution rates without a new vote in the Assembly.
  • Several other municipal, tax and sector-specific laws are adjusted for consistency with these changes.

26771:
• This bill merges, abolishes or reorganizes several public bodies to simplify government administration.
  • It also tightens the rules for senior officials appointed by the government.
Part 1 Health and social services
  • Merges the Institut national d'excellence en santé et en services sociaux and the Institut national de santé publique into one body, the Institut québécois de santé et de services sociaux.
  • Some functions of these two institutes move to Santé Québec or to the Minister of Health.
  • Urgences-santé's board of directors becomes the same as Santé Québec's board.
  • Héma-Québec, which manages blood donations, takes over the coordination of organ donations, removed from Transplant Québec.
  • Santé Québec will provide administrative services to Urgences-santé.
Part 2 College education
  • Removes the Commission d'évaluation de l'enseignement collégial, which assessed the quality of CEGEPs.
Part 3 International relations
  • Integrates the Office Québec-Monde pour la jeunesse directly into the Ministry of International Relations and La Francophonie.
  • Reorganizes the internal workings of the Office franco-québécois pour la jeunesse.
Part 4 Francophonie
  • Turns the Centre de la francophonie des Amériques into a non-profit organization, governed by the Companies Act.
  • Gives the Minister of the French Language new responsibilities related to Canadian Francophonie.
Part 5 Parental insurance
  • Removes the Conseil de gestion de l'assurance parentale.
  • Transfers management of the parental insurance plan and its fund to Retraite Québec.
Part 6 Finance and environment
  • Requires the Minister of Finance to present a comprehensive financial plan to fight climate change in the budget speech.
  • Allows the government to decide, through a rule with no new vote, how to split the surplus of the Fonds d'électrification et de changements climatiques between the Generations Fund and the land transportation fund.
Part 7 Public funds
  • Removes the Information Technology Fund of the Ministry of Employment and Social Solidarity and transfers its money to the consolidated revenue fund.
  • Also removes Fund 3 for university excellence and performance, with the same transfer.
  • Merges the Fonds d'aide à l'action communautaire autonome and the Fonds québécois d'initiatives sociales into a single fund.
Part 8 Public service
  • Removes the Commission de la fonction publique and transfers its functions to the Administrative Labour Tribunal.
Part 9 Financial markets
  • The Administrative Tribunal of Québec will provide administrative services to the Financial Markets Administrative Tribunal.
  • Requires the Autorité des marchés financiers, which oversees financial institutions, to make certain data available online.
Part 10 Agricultural products
  • Reduces the number of vice-presidents and members needed for certain decisions at the Régie des marchés agricoles et alimentaires du Québec.
Part 11 Auto insurance
  • The government will now appoint the vice-presidents of the Société de l'assurance automobile du Québec and set their salaries.
Part 12 Crown corporations
  • Requires a discussion before a National Assembly committee, at least every four years, on the management of the head of Hydro-Québec, the Commission de la construction du Québec and other Crown corporations.
Part 13 Accountability of senior officials
  • Specifies that senior officials must act with prudence, efficiency and fairness in their work.
  • Imposes a two-year probationary period for anyone appointed as a senior official.
  • During this probationary period, the government can dismiss a senior official who was not already a permanent public servant, with simple 15-day written notice.
Part 14 Public contracts
  • Removes the requirement to regularly renew authorizations to contract with the government.
  • Contracts of the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales will be subject to the same rules as those of government enterprises.
Part 15 Housing
  • Allows housing offices to be merged and new ones created for any territory chosen by the government.
  • Ends the joint management of contributions paid to the Société d'habitation du Québec by certain organizations.
Part 16 Administrative relief
  • Reduces the frequency of certain reports and removes the requirement to produce several documents, including financial reports.
Part 17 Miscellaneous
  • Also contains technical adjustments related to sustainable development, the chief forester and pay equity.
  • Amends many other laws for consistency to reflect these organizational changes.

• Changes the way the 125 members are elected: the National Assembly would grow to 129 seats.
  • Québec would be divided into 80 ridings and 17 electoral regions.
  • 80 seats would be awarded as before, to the candidate who gets the most votes in their riding.
  • 49 other seats would be awarded based on the votes parties get across each region.
  • Each voter would vote twice: once for a riding candidate, once for a regional list.
  • A party must get at least 4% of the votes in Québec to be entitled to regional seats.
  • Parties would have to present as many women as men on their regional lists, alternating.
  • For riding candidates, parties would have to present between 40% and 60% women.
  • Party and election campaign financing rules would be adjusted for this new system, without changing the total budget.
  • Rules would set out how to replace a member if a regional seat becomes vacant during a term.

• This bill creates two new acts and amends several others to strengthen public safety and people's sense of security.
  • It sets rules for disclosing information about certain sex offenders, limits the right to protest near elected officials' homes, and also affects police, access to information, and the correctional system.
Part 1 Act respecting the public disclosure of information concerning certain sex offenders at high risk of reoffending
  • Creates a committee that decides whether information about a sex offender should be made public.
Part 2 Act respecting the public disclosure of information concerning certain sex offenders
  • The Sûreté du Québec and Correctional Services must give the committee information about these offenders.
  • The government can define, through a rule without a new vote, who counts as a targeted "sex offender."
  • Information made public stays available for up to three years.
  • A targeted sex offender can challenge the decision before the Administrative Tribunal of Québec.
  • The Sûreté du Québec must release the information according to the decision made, and keep it updated.
Part 3 Act to promote peace, order, and public safety in Québec
  • Bans protesting within 50 metres of the home of an MNA, a municipally elected official, or an elected warden.
  • Bans possessing or throwing objects or substances that could injure, threaten, or intimidate during a protest.
  • Lets a police officer search a person and their surroundings if they believe the person has such an object, and seize it.
  • Bans, with some exceptions, publicly displaying an object identifying an entity listed on a "criminal intent" list created by the minister.
Part 4 Police Act
  • Lets the minister decide which gendarmerie services can be shared between police forces.
  • Lets police forces share other policing services with each other.
  • Creates Indigenous police boards that can manage a police force shared by several communities.
  • Lets a board enter into an agreement with the government to set up or keep an Indigenous police force in its territory.
Part 5 Act respecting access to documents held by public bodies and the protection of personal information
  • Lets a police force share personal information with an organization or a victim, in certain cases.
Part 6 Private Security Act
  • Changes the rules on the term of office of members of the board of directors of the Bureau de la sécurité privée.
Part 7 Act respecting the Québec correctional system
  • Lets a victim read their own written submissions themselves at certain hearings of the Commission québécoise des libérations conditionnelles.
  • The bill also makes related changes, for consistency, to the Highway Safety Code, the Tobacco Tax Act, the Act respecting administrative justice, and the Consumer Protection Act.

26993:
• The bill simplifies the operating rules of professional orders and expands what certain health professionals can do.
  • It also changes the rules between pharmacists, manufacturers and pharmacy chains.
Part 1 Professional Code
  • Professional orders will be able to adopt certain regulations without the approval of the government or the Office des professions.
  • The Office des professions, which oversees professional orders, will now approve codes of ethics, instead of the government.
  • The Office des professions will decide which diplomas give access to a professional permit, with the government's approval.
  • The Office des professions will have to create a common rule for all orders to settle disagreements over professionals' bills.
  • The Office des professions will be able to create rules that apply to one or more orders at once.
  • The Office des professions alone will set the ethics rules for members of the orders' boards of directors, and will be able to investigate and impose sanctions.
  • The public register of professionals (the roll) will have to include more information about each member.
  • The minimum number of members needed to request a special general meeting is changing.
Part 2 Act respecting nurses
  • Nurses will be able to start examinations and tests in more situations, not just in public health.
  • They will also be able to prescribe examinations, medications, other substances, products and dressings, according to rules yet to come.
  • The rule that reserved the right to vote at general meetings to section delegates only is being removed.
Part 3 Act respecting midwives
  • Midwives will be able to prescribe and provide contraceptive methods more often.
  • They will be able to screen for and treat sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections more broadly, even without symptoms if the test is positive.
Part 4 Act respecting optometry
  • Optometrists will have fewer restrictions on the medications they can prescribe and the care they can provide.
  • Dietitians-nutritionists will see their scope of practice expanded and will no longer need a medical prescription for certain restricted activities.
Part 5 Psychotherapy
  • The Interdisciplinary Advisory Council on Psychotherapy will cease operations.
  • Marriage and family therapists will be able to practise psychotherapy without a special permit, like psychologists and doctors.
  • Students in training will be able to carry out certain psychotherapist activities, if authorized by the Office des professions.
  • People holding a permit from another Canadian province will be able to more easily obtain a psychotherapist permit in Québec.
Part 6 Act respecting agronomists
  • The definition of the profession of agronomist no longer requires that an act be paid for it to count as practising the profession.
Part 7 Pharmacy Act
  • The government will be able to allow a pharmacist to prescribe or substitute a medication with one made by a company in which they have a financial interest, under certain conditions.
Part 8 Act respecting prescription drug insurance
  • A drug manufacturer will be able to pay certain benefits to an intermediary, such as a banner or pharmacy chain.
  • A regulation is also being amended to allow a manufacturer to pay these same benefits to a drug wholesaler.
  • Several other professional acts (notaries, lawyers, land surveyors, denturologists, medical imaging technologists) receive technical, related adjustments linked to these changes.

27679:
• The bill creates a new right allowing a person who is worried to obtain information about an intimate partner who may pose a risk to their safety.
  • It establishes a comprehensive process involving the Sûreté du Québec and a designated body to handle these requests and disclose the information.
  • New act respecting the disclosure of information: a person at risk, or someone acting on their behalf with their consent, may request information about their intimate partner.
  • New act: a minor aged 14 or over may submit such a request on their own.
  • New act: the government may, by regulation, designate other persons or categories of persons who may submit a request.
  • New act: police officers and workers from support organizations may inform a person at risk about the request process if it could benefit them.
  • New act: a police officer may, in these cases, disclose the identity of the partner who is the subject of a possible request.
  • New act: the Sûreté du Québec conducts the searches and transmits the relevant information to a body designated by the minister responsible for the status of women.
  • New act: a designated person, subject to regulatory conditions, meets with the person at risk to verbally communicate the information or the absence of relevant information.
  • New act: this person may also direct the person at risk to specialized resources and provide additional information.
  • New act: restrictions govern the disclosure to the intimate partner of the existence of a request and personal information concerning them.
  • New act: rules limit the further communication and use of the information obtained.
  • New act: certain persons benefit from immunity for acts performed in the exercise of their duties related to this process.
  • New act: these persons cannot be compelled to testify before a court concerning this information.
  • New act: penal offences are provided for breaches of the rules on communication or use of information.
  • Act respecting the Québec correctional system: revises the rules on disclosing to victims information concerning incarcerated persons or those under the supervision of correctional services.
  • Act respecting the Ministère de la Sécurité publique: consequential adjustments related to the creation of the new information disclosure regime.

27695:
• Creates a mandatory "co-construction" process with First Nations and Inuit for laws and regulations that concern them.
  • Requires a preliminary analysis to determine whether a measure affects them, before initiating co-construction.
